meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, Hale. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Now the basis, Hale: what do you actually have?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.

Show me the note, Hale, the one you wrote that day. A seventeen-year-old fumbling a definition when his teacher springs it on him proves nothing about who wrote the essay. Was he told, on November 2, that his mark depended on what he said?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

I'm writing down October 15. Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's what outlines are for. Put the outline and your November 2 note on the table where I can read them.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

That's your own procedure 4.4, Hale, not a favour, and I still haven't seen a single page of what you've told me. "If it holds up," judged by whom, and on what standard? Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, so show me the outline and the note before I agree to anything.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you acknowledged entering the zero before contacting me, and you offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require copies of Owen's October 15 outline and your November 2 note, and a written assurance that this stays off his record and is handled privately. I expect your offer in writing by Friday at 3 PM, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position; she agreed to nothing yet and still wants to see the outline and the note, and a promise that this stays private and off Owen's record, before she considers the rewrite.
What moved her: owning the early zero in one clean sentence and moving on, then citing dated, specific moments from Owen's own work, because she trusts procedure and dates over impressions.
What cost ground: nothing cost real ground, though describing the outline and note without showing them kept her from moving further, because she only moves on documents she can check herself.
Try next time: when you brought up the October 15 outline, put it and your November 2 note in front of her to read before making the rewrite offer.
